clue.text: Doctor unclear about soldier in pain

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the soldier
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: GI is the usual crossword abbreviation for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A medic who speaks unclearly is treating a soldier suffering from pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is the anagram signal: UNCLEAR becomes NEURALC, and 'about' wraps those letters round GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgic describes the sharp nerve pain called neuralgia, so a sufferer is in pain.

clue.text: Teachers collectively breed a kind of bird

parts.note: the NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union speaking for teachers as a body
to breed young birds is to hatch them

explanation.surface: Teachers as a body are rearing a particular bird species.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT, the National Union of Teachers, is a British teachers' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small songbird that climbs tree trunks head first.

clue.text: Like diamonds, initially, or complete pack

explanation.surface: Diamonds at the start of play, or the full deck of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at the diamond suit in cards; in fact gems are rough before cutting, and a pack nobody has cut is still whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemstones come from the ground rough before a cutter shapes them; a deck of cards not yet divided by a player stays entire.

clue.text: So romantic about friend on a huge scale

indicators.note: about here means knocked about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone is enormously romantic towards a close companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SO ROMANTIC into ASTRONOMIC, then ALLY follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomical figures are vast, so the adverb means to an enormous degree.

clue.text: Vivid Greek account, full of Hellenic character

indicators.note: full of says the account abbreviation holds the letter inside it

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A colourful Greek narrative packed with characters from Hellas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hellenic character' is a letter of the Greek alphabet, not a person in the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A graphic description is lively and detailed, painting a clear picture.

clue.text: Sailor was exultant on island

parts.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast or exult
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: A seaman was jubilant once he reached land.
explanation.walkthrough: CREW is the old past tense of 'crow' (to exult), as in 'the cock crew'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crewman is a member of a ship's company, a seaman.

clue.text: Divine part of good intention

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something holy forms a share of a well-meant aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' is read as a noun, a deity, rather than an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology, so he is a divinity.

clue.text: Composer repeated it with dozen changes

indicators.note: changes signals that the pooled letters are put in a new order
repeated says the little word is written out twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician played a piece over again, with twelve alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: ITIT plus DOZEN gives nine letters which 'changes' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaetano Donizetti was an Italian opera writer, of Lucia di Lammermoor fame.

clue.text: Sensing absence of wickedness? Good

parts.note: no sin is a lack of wickedness

explanation.surface: Someone detects that there is no evil present and approves.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO SIN + G.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosing out something means sniffing or detecting it, as an animal does by smell.

clue.text: Never ruminate wildly about upper class, it's not rewarding

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the class letter
wildly says the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: U stands for upper-class usage in British English

explanation.surface: Advice not to brood frantically over the posh set, since it pays nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges NEVER RUMINATE, and 'about' puts it round U, the British label for upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: Unremunerative work brings no pay or profit.

clue.text: After pet returns, it's taken for granted

indicators.note: after says the next piece follows the turned pet
returns means the pet word comes back reading right to left

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet
the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Once the family animal comes home, it is assumed all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: CAT turned back by 'returns' gives TAC, and 'After' puts IT behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is understood without being said, so it is assumed.

clue.text: A writer's occupied by Muses, say, in mountain range

indicators.note: occupied by means the pen word is filled by the number

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool, and the possessive adds S
there were nine Muses in Greek myth, so they are an example of the number

explanation.surface: An author's work taken over by inspiring goddesses in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Muses, Greek goddesses of the arts, were nine in number.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the chain of mountains running down the length of Italy.

clue.text: Against old church where Christian was first employed

parts.note: anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: Opposed to an ancient church where a believer first got a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed' means used as a word: Acts 11:26 says the disciples were first called Christians at this city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible records that followers of Jesus were first given the name Christian in this Syrian city.

clue.text: One of towering authority in Islam?

definitions.text: One of towering authority in Islam?

parts.words: One of towering authority in Islam?
parts.note: towering is literal: the person calls the faithful to prayer from high up a minaret, not someone of great rank

explanation.walkthrough: 'towering authority' suggests a powerful leader; the clue means someone whose post is literally high up a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A muezzin is the mosque official who gives the call to prayer from the minaret.

clue.text: How to behave, having caught rival medic turning on channel

indicators.note: turning means the rival and medic words are read together right to left

parts.note: a foe is an opponent or rival
doc is a short word for a doctor
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a duct is a channel or pipe

explanation.surface: A guide to manners, having nabbed a competing doctor switching over a TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses FOE DOC as a run, giving CODEOF.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of rules for conduct tells people the proper way to act.

clue.text: Old money I spread out, on show

parts.note: D stood for a penny in Britain's pre-decimal currency
splayed means spread wide apart

explanation.surface: Someone lays out their old coins for everyone to see.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the old British penny, from the Latin denarius.
explanation.definitionFit: Something displayed is exhibited for people to see.

clue.text: Holy beginner, type one converted

indicators.note: converted means the letters are changed into a new order
beginner points to the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A novice in religion is described as a sort of person who has been converted.
explanation.walkthrough: &lit: H from the start of 'Holy' plus TYPE ONE are rearranged by 'converted', and the whole clue also describes a new convert.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a newcomer to a faith, a novice or recent proselyte.

clue.text: Vessel South of equator, carrying fruit

indicators.note: carrying means the south-of-equator phrase holds the fruit inside it

parts.note: taken as written
sailors call the equator the Line
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: A boat below the equator, loaded with produce.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors call the equator 'the Line', so 'South of equator' is S OF THE LINE, and 'carrying' takes HIP after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship of the line was a large warship fit to fight in the line of battle.

clue.text: Have something in common about friend turning up

parts.note: over can mean about, as in fretting over a problem

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the friend word from bottom to top

parts.note: pal is an informal word for a friend

explanation.surface: Share some interest when a mate arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' looks like arriving, but in a down answer it reverses PAL to LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that overlap share part of their extent.

clue.text: Trooped off to attack ship

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and need putting in a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers marched away to assault a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TROOPED; 'attack ship' is a verb phrase, to hit a ship with a missile.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo is to strike a vessel with an underwater missile.

clue.text: Not telling on others, as an American family value?

definitions.text: Not telling on others, as an American family value?

parts.words: Not telling on others, as an American family value?
parts.note: the family is the Mafia, and the value is the code of silence that forbids informing to the police

explanation.walkthrough: 'family value' suggests wholesome homes; the clue means a crime family's rule against informing.
explanation.definitionFit: Omertà is the Mafia's code of silence, which forbids cooperating with the authorities.

clue.text: On motorway, league's non-U distance

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, its 1 read as I

indicators.note: non-U means the letter U is removed from the league word

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: On the motorway, the football league is not upper class over distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; its figure 1 stands for the letter I. 'non-U' also means not upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: Mileage is a distance travelled, counted in miles.

clue.text: What unfolds as travel plans are made?

definitions.text: What unfolds as travel plans are made?

parts.words: What unfolds as travel plans are made?
parts.note: unfolds is literal: a folded paper guide to the routes is opened out while the trip is planned

explanation.walkthrough: 'unfolds' reads as 'develops', but here it is a folded paper chart being opened.
explanation.definitionFit: A road map is a chart of routes for drivers, usually folded.

clue.text: Filthy ferry finally seen south of Scottish island

indicators.note: in a down clue south of means placed below the island

parts.note: Muck is a small island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A dirty ferry is spotted at last off a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: Muck is one of Scotland's Small Isles; Y goes beneath it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mucky is dirty, covered in grime.

clue.text: VIP unhappy, put in shade

parts.note: a royal is a very important person
blue means sad

explanation.surface: An important person, upset, is pushed into the background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in shade' suggests being overshadowed; 'shade' is the definition, a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep, vivid hue of blue.

clue.text: Saying nasty things, biting head off, making you want to scratch

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is cut from the spiteful word

parts.note: bitchy describes spiteful, cutting remarks

explanation.surface: Being spiteful and sharp, and also causing an urge to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: BITCHY loses its first letter by 'head off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy skin causes an irritating urge to rub.

clue.text: Some grand young man's name

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fine youngster's moniker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young man' reads as one phrase, but only 'man's name' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy is a familiar short form of Andrew, a boy's given name.

clue.text: Convert for unorthodox Ely set

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: unorthodox says the letters are put in an irregular order

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: A churchman switches allegiance because of a heterodox group in Ely.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire; 'unorthodox' rearranges ELY SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A proselyte is someone newly converted to a religion or cause.
